providers.byoi_notes: ARM64 not supported via VM Import/Export. i386 support ends 2026-04-01. Upload to S3 then call ec2 import-image. FreeBSD requires manual AMI build or bsdec2-image-upload tool (BSD-licensed).
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload image to S3, call ec2:ImportImage API. FreeBSD 14.x official AMIs published by FreeBSD RE team to AWS Marketplace and SSM Parameter Store (/aws/service/freebsd/...).
providers.tooling_license: AWS CLI: Apache-2.0. bsdec2-image-upload: BSD-2-Clause (safe to vendor).
providers.notes: No direct ISO boot. ARM64 import blocked by VM Import/Export. Free-tier FreeBSD AMIs available. Official AMIs for amd64 and aarch64 from FreeBSD RE.

providers.byoi_notes: Must convert to RAW (disk.raw) and tar.gz before upload. VMDK supported via import pipeline. Boot disk size increments of 1 GB. Requires MBR or hybrid GPT/MBR partition table.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload tar.gz of raw disk image to Cloud Storage, then call compute.images.insert API. FreeBSD images maintained in freebsd-org-cloud-dev GCP project by FreeBSD community.
providers.tooling_license: gcloud CLI: Apache-2.0 (safe to invoke as external tool).
providers.notes: FreeBSD 14.0+ has gVNIC preview support. Images not in default public project; must reference freebsd-org-cloud-dev. qcow2 not directly importable; must convert to raw.

providers.byoi_notes: Only fixed-size VHD accepted (not VHDX, not dynamic VHD). Gen2 VM requires VHD with UEFI. Upload to Azure Blob Storage then create managed disk. VHDX must be converted to VHD first.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload fixed-size VHD to Azure Blob Storage via azcopy/az CLI, create managed disk, then create VM image. FreeBSD 13.5 published to Azure Marketplace by FreeBSD Foundation.
providers.tooling_license: az CLI: MIT (safe to invoke). azcopy: MIT.
providers.notes: Gen2 VMs use UEFI. FreeBSD in Azure Marketplace (Foundation-maintained, Q1 2025: 13.5-RELEASE). VHDX format not supported for upload despite being native to Hyper-V. Root account disabled by default in Azure FreeBSD images.

providers.byoi_notes: Images exported as .oci (qcow2 + metadata). FreeBSD requires emulated mode launch, not paravirtualized. Kernel must be patched for OCI. Paravirtualized requires Linux kernel 3.4+.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload qcow2/vmdk to Object Storage bucket, import via OCI console or CLI as custom image. FreeBSD arm64 available in OCI Marketplace since FreeBSD 13.1. x86 BYOI in emulated mode.
providers.tooling_license: oci-cli: Apache-2.0 (safe to invoke). Terraform OCI provider: MPL-2.0.
providers.notes: Free tier includes 4 OCPUs Ampere A1 (aarch64) - popular for FreeBSD. BYOI not supported on bare metal directly. OCI exports use .oci container format wrapping qcow2.

providers.byoi_notes: Image must be uploaded to OSS bucket first. Supports custom images via ImportImage API. FreeBSD 13+ public images include kernel patches for 5th-gen+ instance families.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload image to Alibaba Cloud OSS, call ECS ImportImage API. Official FreeBSD public images available with patched kernels for Alibaba hypervisor compatibility.
providers.notes: FreeBSD 11/12 require kernel patches not included in upstream builds. Public FreeBSD images are Alibaba-maintained with patches. Primary audience is China market.

providers.byoi_notes: Upload to COS bucket, import via console or API. FreeBSD listed as supported OS. ISO import supported for Linux-family only via separate ISO import path.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload image to Tencent Cloud Object Storage (COS), import via CVM ImportImage API. FreeBSD available as stock image. ISO Linux import also available.
providers.notes: Primary market China. International portal (intl.cloud.tencent.com) differs from domestic. FreeBSD availability in international region not fully confirmed - staleness risk.

providers.byoi_notes: Upload to IBM Cloud Object Storage, import via VPC API. BYOL supported. Stock images: RHEL, Ubuntu, Windows, Debian, Rocky, Fedora, SUSE. No FreeBSD stock image.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload qcow2 or VHD to IBM Cloud Object Storage, import via VPC instances API. No FreeBSD stock image; custom import required for BSD.
providers.notes: Power Systems (ppc64le) available via IBM Power Virtual Server - separate product. Classic Infrastructure (non-VPC) has different image requirements. No native BSD support in stock catalog.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom ISO upload via URL (public URL required, max 2 per account, max 10 GB). ISO must be bootable. No raw/qcow2 direct import; ISO only. FreeBSD available as stock image.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Provide public URL for custom ISO; Vultr downloads and stores it. Attach ISO to instance for boot install. FreeBSD 14.x available as managed stock image with KVM and VirtIO drivers.
providers.notes: Best FreeBSD experience among mid-tier providers as of 2025. Stock images use UFS root. IPv6 available in all 33 regions. No aarch64 compute available. Max 2 custom ISOs per account.

providers.byoi_notes: Image provided as public URL or uploaded to Spaces. Must have ext3/ext4 filesystem. cloud-init 0.7.7+ or bsd-cloudinit required. Images can be gzip or bzip2 compressed.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: POST to /v2/images with image URL or upload via Spaces. FreeBSD dropped as stock OS April 2022; custom image upload required. API-driven custom image import available.
providers.notes: CRITICAL: FreeBSD dropped from stock images July 2022. Must use custom image path. No aarch64 for custom images. Requires bsd-cloudinit for FreeBSD custom images. Max 100 GB uncompressed.

providers.byoi_notes: Raw .img only (optionally gzipped). Must be ext3 or ext4 filesystem. Not partitioned (unpartitioned preferred). Max compressed 5 GB, uncompressed 6 GB. 25 images max, 150 GB total.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload raw disk image via API PUT to signed URL. FreeBSD NOT officially supported; custom raw images can be uploaded but unsupported and ext3/ext4 requirement limits BSD UFS/ZFS use.
providers.notes: CRITICAL: FreeBSD not officially supported. Only ext3/ext4 accepted - rules out UFS and ZFS natively. Max 6 GB uncompressed is very small for BSD images with packages. Aarch64 available for instances but not confirmed for custom image upload.

providers.byoi_notes: No official direct image upload API. Workaround: spin up server, dd raw image over existing disk, snapshot. Community tool hcloud-upload-image automates this. Official method: Packer builder builds image in-place and snapshots.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: No official BYOI. Create server with rescue OS, stream raw image to disk, take snapshot via API. hcloud-upload-image tool (MIT licensed) automates the process. FreeBSD not a stock image.
providers.tooling_license: hcloud CLI: MIT. hcloud-upload-image: MIT (safe to vendor).
providers.notes: No native image upload endpoint as of 2026-04. hcloud-upload-image is community-supported, not official. FreeBSD deployable via workaround. ARM64 (CAX) instances available. IPv6 standard on all servers.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom images via installimage script. tar.gz archive format. Officially supports Archlinux, Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL-compatible only for custom images. FreeBSD via KVM console ISO boot (manual).
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Boot into Hetzner rescue system, use installimage script or manually stream OS from custom tar.gz. FreeBSD requires KVM console ISO install; no automated FreeBSD path. Hetzner dropped FreeBSD rescue system.
providers.tooling_license: Robot API: REST, no SDK license issues.
providers.notes: Hetzner dropped FreeBSD rescue system - FreeBSD install now requires KVM console (paid add-on) or USB stick on request. Custom image installimage officially Linux-only. No Hetzner support for custom installs.

providers.byoi_notes: Import snapshot from qcow2 in Object Storage. Must use .qcow or .qcow2 extension. Must use EFI boot (not BIOS only). Volume size 1 GB - 1 TB. Snapshot in same region as bucket.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload qcow2 to Scaleway Object Storage bucket, import as snapshot via API or console. Convert snapshot to image for deployment. EFI boot required for imported images.
providers.notes: EFI-only for imported images is a hard constraint - BIOS-only BSD images will not boot. No FreeBSD in stock image catalog. Apple Silicon M1/M4/M4 Pro available as dedicated bare-metal Mac mini.

providers.byoi_notes: OpenStack-based. Upload via OpenStack CLI or Horizon. Recommends raw or qcow2. cloud-init and QEMU Guest Agent recommended for cloud-readiness.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: OpenStack-compatible. Upload image to Glance (Object Storage via Swift), boot instance. OpenStack CLI or Horizon web UI. BYOI for Public Cloud separate from dedicated server BYOI.
providers.notes: OpenStack under the hood gives broad compatibility. Dedicated server BYOI (separate product) supports raw/qcow2 for bare metal. Docs updated Feb 2026.

providers.byoi_notes: Dedicated server BYOI streams image URL to bare metal. Supports raw and qcow2. cloud-init recommended. API or control panel deployment.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Provide public URL to raw/qcow2 image. OVH boots server into netboot, streams image to disk. API-driven via OVH APIv6 or control panel. Docs updated Feb 2026.
providers.tooling_license: OVH API: REST, no SDK license concerns. ovh-cli: MIT.
providers.notes: Separate product from OVHcloud Public Cloud. Full bare-metal BYOI with cloud-init for FreeBSD viable. Dedibox (dedicated) also supports FreeBSD as a stock install option.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom Images add-on required (purchased at time of ordering). Supports ISO and qcow2. Must be x86-64 (amd64 only). VirtIO drivers required (virtio_scsi for disk, virtio_net for networking).
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Upload ISO or qcow2 via customer panel or Contabo API after purchasing Custom Images add-on. Deploy VM from custom image in any Contabo location via web UI or API.
providers.tooling_license: Contabo API: REST. No open-source SDK noted.
providers.notes: Custom Images is a paid add-on, not included by default. amd64 only - no aarch64. qcow2 treated as pre-installed disk image. Very budget-oriented; lower SLA than Tier 1.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom iPXE boot: provide public URL to iPXE script that chainloads your image. FreeBSD and other BSDs deployable this way. SERVICE SUNSETS JUNE 30, 2026.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Provision bare metal with Custom iPXE option; provide public iPXE script URL. Metal loads iPXE which chainloads your OS. FreeBSD available as stock managed OS. Full bare-metal control.
providers.notes: CRITICAL: Equinix Metal sunsets June 30, 2026. No new commercial sales. Do NOT build new genoa adapters for this target. Existing users should migrate. Alternatives: Hivelocity, phoenixNAP, Latitude.sh.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom iPXE support: provide iPXE script URL at provisioning time. API-driven. Full bare metal access via IPMI. Custom OS via iPXE chainload or IPMI remote console.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Provision via Hivelocity API selecting Custom iPXE OS option. Provide public iPXE script URL. Terraform provider available. IPMI credentials provided for manual console access.
providers.notes: Instant-deploy server catalog. Global locations. Proxmox deployable. FreeBSD installable via iPXE or IPMI console. No aarch64 compute.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom OS via cloud-init or Custom OS option. API, CLI, and IaC (Terraform) support. Bare metal provisioned in minutes. Custom OS and cloud-init documented.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: API-driven bare metal cloud. Select operating system at provision time. Custom OS option via cloud-init. Instances billed hourly or by reservation. Multiple data center locations.
providers.notes: BMC = Bare Metal Cloud product. Strong API and IaC story. Custom OS details not fully public-documented without account. FreeBSD not listed as stock OS - custom path required.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom ISO installable via SolusVM control panel (CDROM tab). FreeBSD available on KVM VPS. Very reputable for BSD hosting.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: SolusVM control panel provides CDROM/ISO selection for KVM instances. FreeBSD available as template. Custom ISO can be mounted for custom installs.
providers.tooling_license: SolusVM API: proprietary panel, REST API available.
providers.notes: Budget-oriented but reputable. KVM only for BSD. OpenVZ VPS does not support BSD. FreeBSD and other BSDs deployable with full virtualization.

providers.byoi_notes: KVM-based. FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFlyBSD available as templates. Custom ISO support via Stallion panel. BSD available on KVM only (not OpenVZ).
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Stallion/KVM control panel for ISO mounting and OS selection. BSD distros available as pre-built templates. Custom ISO can be loaded for additional BSDs. Las Vegas, New York, Luxembourg locations.
providers.tooling_license: No public API documented. Stallion panel is proprietary.
providers.notes: Well-regarded budget BSD provider. DDoS protection included. No public API for automation. Stock BSD images may be older versions (FreeBSD 9/10/11, OpenBSD 6 per docs - check for updates).

providers.byoi_notes: No BYOI. Lambda provides fixed base images: Lambda Stack (Ubuntu + NVIDIA/CUDA/ML frameworks), GPU Base (minimal), Ubuntu Server (bare). Cannot import custom OS images.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Select from Lambda-provided Ubuntu-based images. GPU instances with NVIDIA A100, H100, etc. No custom OS support. Target audience: ML/AI workloads only.
providers.notes: BYOI: none. BSD: none. GPU specialist. No custom image path exists. Not suitable for genoa unless targeting ML workloads on Lambda-provided Ubuntu.

providers.byoi_notes: Kubernetes-native. Deploy custom container images or VMs via KubeVirt. Custom VM images (qcow2/raw) can be imported as PVCs. GPU-focused; NVIDIA A100/H100/H200 available.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Kubernetes (KubeVirt) orchestration. Custom VM images importable as PersistentVolumeClaims. Container images from any OCI registry. Primarily used for ML training/inference workloads.
providers.notes: KubeVirt path makes FreeBSD theoretically deployable but not validated. Primarily GPU/ML workloads. No BSD stock images. Documentation requires account access to verify BYOI details.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom Docker/OCI container images only. Pull from Docker Hub, ECR, GHCR, etc. 10 GB pull limit via registry. Larger via volume mounts. Not a VM image - container only.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Specify Docker image name when creating Pod. RunPod pulls OCI image and runs in KVM-backed container environment. GPU access passed through. No arbitrary OS/VM image support.
providers.notes: Container-only BYOI, not VM image. BSD not deployable. GPU Pod model; suitable for ML workloads only from genoa perspective. Not a VM deploy target for BSD/custom OS images.

providers.byoi_notes: Gradient Notebooks and Deployments accept custom Docker containers. Machines product supports custom VM templates cloned from existing Machines. No raw OS image import.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Gradient: deploy Docker containers on GPU instances. Machines: Linux/Windows VMs with persistent storage, custom templates by cloning. No BYOI raw image path. Acquired by DigitalOcean.
providers.notes: Machines product supports custom templates but only from cloning existing Linux/Windows VMs. BSD not deployable. GPU specialist. Gradient = container-only path.

providers.byoi_notes: VM instances with persistent storage volumes. Custom image import via API (details require account). Primarily Ubuntu-based GPU workloads. Sustainable/renewable energy focus.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: VM GPU instances with custom disk images. Kubernetes and standalone VM modes. Primarily ML/AI workloads. Custom image path exists but documentation sparse without account.
providers.notes: Renewable/stranded energy focus differentiator. Custom image support likely but unconfirmed for BSD without account access. GPU H100/A100 focus. Small provider, growing.

providers.byoi_notes: Docker/OCI container images only. Fly converts Docker images to Firecracker microVM root filesystems. No raw disk image or ISO support. BSD: out of scope.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Deploy Docker/OCI container images; Fly.io converts to Firecracker microVMs internally. No arbitrary OS image support. Machines API controls VM lifecycle.
providers.notes: OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. Docker-only ingestion. Firecracker VMs are internal implementation. No path for arbitrary OS images. Global anycast edge.

providers.byoi_notes: Serverless JS/WASM isolates only. No VM, no OS, no filesystem. Cannot accept any VM image. Out of scope.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: JavaScript/TypeScript/WASM isolates deployed to edge. No virtual machine abstraction. No OS concept. Not a VM deployment target.
providers.notes: OUT OF SCOPE. No VM capability at all. Isolate model (V8). No OS, no filesystem persistence, no BSD or Linux. Cloudflare Images product is CDN image optimization, not VM images.

providers.byoi_notes: Deploy via Docker/OCI container images or Git+Dockerfile build. No raw VM image or ISO support. Linux containers only. BSD: out of scope.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Deploy Docker prebuilt images or Dockerfile builds from Git. Managed Kubernetes infrastructure. No arbitrary OS image support. Web services, static sites, databases only.
providers.notes: OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. Docker-only. No VM image ingestion. No custom OS.

providers.byoi_notes: Docker image or Dockerfile/Nixpacks build from Git. No VM image import. Container-only deployment.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Deploy from Docker image (Docker Hub, GHCR, Quay, GitLab CR) or auto-build via Nixpacks/Dockerfile. No raw OS image path.
providers.notes: OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. Container-only.

providers.byoi_notes: Container/Kubernetes platform. BYOC (Bring Your Own Cloud) means connect your AWS/GCP/Azure cluster, not OS images. Deploy OCI containers only. Kata Containers/gVisor for isolation.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Deploy OCI containers on Northflank-managed or customer-provided Kubernetes clusters. BYOC brings cloud account not OS images.
providers.notes: OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. BYOC != BYOI. Container-only for workload deployment.

providers.byoi_notes: Firecracker microVM-backed. Accepts Dockerfile or prebuilt Docker/OCI images. No VM disk image import. BSD: out of scope.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Deploy Docker/Dockerfile to Firecracker microVMs. Global edge deployment. Scale-to-zero. No arbitrary OS image path.
providers.notes: OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. Interesting architecture (Firecracker + Nomad) but container-only interface. No BYOI path.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom OS image loading supported. KVM/QEMU with Ceph storage. FreeBSD and OpenBSD native support since 2008. IPv6 block included. Custom kernel compilation supported.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: KVM/QEMU VPS with Ceph storage backend. FreeBSD and OpenBSD as managed templates. Custom OS image loading possible. Native IPv6 block per customer.
providers.tooling_license: Custom API, no known SDK license issues.
providers.notes: FreeBSD/OpenBSD specialist since 2008. Small but highly BSD-competent. Kernel compilation allowed. ZFS-capable. 10% discount for semi-annual/annual. US-based.

providers.byoi_notes: Xen VPS since 2005. FreeBSD as prebuilt image and netboot install. NetBSD and OpenBSD via netboot install only. NetBSD requires HVM (not PV). Technically adept user base expected.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Xen-based VPS. FreeBSD 14.2 as prebuilt image. OpenBSD 7.8 and NetBSD 10.1 via netboot install. Small provider for BSD-savvy users.
providers.notes: Xen hypervisor (rare among modern providers). Active FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD releases as of Dec 2025. Very small provider. NetBSD only under HVM not PV.

providers.byoi_notes: See buyvm entry. Duplicate entry as Tier 5 for BSD-focused coverage. FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFlyBSD templates.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: KVM VPS with BSD OS templates. See primary buyvm entry.
providers.notes: Duplicate of buyvm for Tier 5 BSD tracking. DDoS protection notable feature. Las Vegas NV, New York NY, Luxembourg locations.

providers.byoi_notes: FreeBSD supported same as Linux VMs: live attach/detach of network interfaces, IP, SSH keys. OpenZFS configured by default. Last two supported FreeBSD releases maintained as templates.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Wholesale IaaS with FreeBSD as first-class citizen. Templates for last two FreeBSD releases. OpenZFS default on FreeBSD templates. Sydney/Australia focus. API-driven.
providers.tooling_license: OrionVM API: REST. No known license issues.
providers.notes: Anthony Woodward appointed chairman March 2025 - active company. Australia-headquartered. FreeBSD on equal footing with Linux. AI infrastructure pivot with Blaize partnership.

providers.byoi_notes: Free BSD VPS for learning/education. No BYOI - uses pre-built templates. FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFlyBSD, and Solaris-family available. 1 vCPU / 1 GB RAM / 10 GB disk free.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Free community BSD VPS platform using Proxmox-backed KVM. Distributed globally. 500+ active BSD VPS. Education/exploration focus. No production SLA.
providers.notes: Free and no credit card required. Not suitable for production genoa deployments. Excellent for FreeBSD/OpenBSD/NetBSD/DragonFlyBSD testing. Proxmox migration announced 2024-2025.

providers.byoi_notes: Raspberry Pi cloud (aarch64 bare metal). Stock OS: Raspberry Pi OS and Ubuntu. No FreeBSD stock image. Custom OS possible via API image parameter. UK-based.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Raspberry Pi cloud: provision Pi 3/Pi 4 nodes via API with choice of OS image. Custom image deployable by specifying image URL in API. ARM64 bare metal.
providers.notes: Unique: Raspberry Pi (aarch64) dedicated nodes as a service. Not VMs - actual Pi hardware. FreeBSD on Pi is possible but not stock. UK-based (Cambridge). From £7.14/mo.

providers.byoi_notes: Dedicated FreeBSD server hosting. San Diego CA. Bare metal and cloud VMs. No minimum term, no setup fee. Custom configurations available via support.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Managed dedicated FreeBSD servers and BSD cloud VMs. San Diego datacenter. Manual provisioning via support team. Not API-automated.
providers.notes: Small specialized provider, FreeBSD and Linux/BSD dedicated servers. Not API-automated. Not suitable for genoa automated dispatch without custom integration. US West Coast only.

providers.byoi_notes: Orka platform: OCI-compliant macOS VM images on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3). Custom macOS images via Orka Desktop (local) or Orka Engine (cloud). macOS only - no BSD/Linux VMs.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Orka platform orchestrates macOS VMs on Apple Silicon hardware. Kubernetes-native (Orka 3.x). OCI-compliant macOS images. API and CLI. Bare metal Mac mini M1/M2/M3 in Atlanta, Las Vegas, Dublin.
providers.tooling_license: Orka CLI: proprietary. Kubernetes integration: Apache-2.0.
providers.notes: Apple Silicon aarch64 only. HVF hypervisor (Apple Hypervisor.framework). macOS-only VMs. Not suitable for BSD/Linux genoa deployments. macOS license requires 24h minimum.

providers.byoi_notes: Dedicated Apple M1/M4/M4 Pro Mac mini nodes. No hypervisor - bare metal macOS. No BYOI - macOS only. 24h minimum lease. €0.22/hour for M4.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Bare metal Apple M1/M4/M4 Pro Mac mini as a service. Dedicated hardware, no hypervisor. macOS only. API/CLI provisioning. VPC integration available.
providers.notes: Launched M4 January 27, 2025. Bare metal - no VMs possible. macOS license: 24h minimum. M4 Pro also available. Not suitable for genoa BSD/Linux deployments.

providers.byoi_notes: Custom macOS AMIs built via EC2 Image Builder (GA October 2024). Only macOS supported. Dedicated Mac mini hardware (M1, M2, M4, M4 Pro). 24h minimum tenancy. AMI = macOS only.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Dedicated Apple Mac mini hardware (M1/M2/M4) in AWS. Launch macOS AMI, create custom AMI from running instance. EC2 Image Builder for macOS AMI pipelines. 24h minimum host lease.
providers.notes: EC2 Image Builder macOS support GA October 2024. Supports Big Sur through Sequoia. Not suitable for FreeBSD/BSD. macOS license requires Dedicated Host (24h minimum). Elastic network adapter support.

providers.byoi_notes: Hetzner offered M1 Mac mini but discontinued the offering. No longer available or upgradeable.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Former service - M1 Mac mini as dedicated server. Discontinued. No longer available for new orders.
providers.notes: DEFUNCT. Hetzner Mac mini M1 discontinued. Cannot upgrade existing. Not orderable. Use MacStadium, Scaleway Apple Silicon, or AWS EC2 Mac instead.

providers.byoi_notes: SmartOS/illumos-based. Zones (OS containers) and KVM VMs. Custom images (imgapi) via Triton. CDDL/MPL-2.0 licensed stack. Unique: zones give near-bare-metal performance with isolation.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Triton DataCenter: provision SmartOS zones or KVM VMs. Custom images via IMGAPI (image management service). MNX Public Cloud available. Private cloud deployment also supported.
providers.tooling_license: Triton CLI: MPL-2.0. SmartOS: CDDL (for OS components). MNX tooling: BSD/MIT/MPL-2.0 mix.
providers.notes: Joyent acquired by Samsung 2016; Triton/SmartOS spun to MNX 2022. Still actively developed. Unique illumos foundation. CDDL components in SmartOS not vendorable (copyleft). BSD zones not natively supported (illumos-based).

providers.byoi_notes: Full native support for all image formats. All architectures via QEMU TCG (software emulation) or KVM (hardware acceleration). libvirt API or direct QEMU CLI.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Direct QEMU/KVM invocation or via libvirt API. All formats supported. All BSDs supported. genoa local target for dev/test. virsh, virt-install, or direct qemu-system-* commands.
providers.tooling_license: QEMU: GPL-2.0 (runtime only - OK to invoke as external tool, NOT to vendor). libvirt: LGPL-2.1 (OK to link dynamically). libguestfs: LGPL-2.1.
providers.notes: CRITICAL LICENSE NOTE: QEMU itself is GPL-2.0; genoa must invoke it as external process not vendor/embed it. libvirt API binding libraries are LGPL. KVM kernel module is GPL-2.0 kernel module (Linux). All formats and BSDs work natively.

providers.byoi_notes: FreeBSD native hypervisor. BSD-licensed. Supports raw, qcow2 (via bhyve), vmdk. UEFI and CSM BIOS. vm-bhyve or cbsd management layers. Linux, FreeBSD, Windows guests.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: FreeBSD kernel hypervisor. Direct bhyve CLI or vm-bhyve/cbsd management tools. Runs on FreeBSD host. All BSDs as guests. Linux (limited) guest support. UEFI via BHYVE_UEFI firmware.
providers.tooling_license: bhyve: BSD-2-Clause (safe to vendor). vm-bhyve: BSD-2-Clause. cbsd: BSD-2-Clause.
providers.notes: IDEAL for genoa: all tools BSD-licensed, safe to vendor. FreeBSD host required. OpenBSD and NetBSD run as guests. Best FreeBSD-native deployment target. Also available on OmniOS/illumos.

providers.byoi_notes: RootBSD was a BSD-specialist hosting company. Now merged into NetActuate. Original brand/service no longer active as independent entity.
providers.deployment_mechanism_summary: Former BSD-focused VPS provider. Redirects to NetActuate. Original service defunct.
providers.notes: DEFUNCT as independent brand. rootbsd.net redirects to NetActuate. Historical BSD-specialist. Check NetActuate for continuation of service.
